caption:
Anxiety. Low mood. A sleep problem. Then, ADHD.

One large study in Japan found many adults had been diagnosed with low mood, a sleep problem or anxiety in the two years before their ADHD diagnosis. Emotional ups and downs and restlessness are common in adult ADHD, and sleep problems often sit alongside it. A careful assessment follows the timeline back to childhood, to understand what came first.

Part of our series, ADHD: the full picture.

Research:
Long, N., & Coats, H. (2022). The need for earlier recognition of ADHD in primary care. https://doi.org/10.1093/fampra/cmac038
Okada, T., et al. (2024). Psychiatric comorbidities of ADHD in Japan: A nationwide population-based study. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2024.1359872
